text:
jordan: heads up --- spotted a CI job stdout paste that contains a long JSON blob with what looks like a Vault token and a GCP service account key id. link: https://paste.internal/abcd (redacted)
sec-oncall: ack. can you paste the exact lines you saw? we need to triage scope before rotating everything.
jordan: sure. snippet below (redacted):
```
{"type":"service_account","private_key_id":"0123abcd...","client_email":"ci-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"}
X-Vault-Token: s.xxxxxx
```
alex: ok first step: disable the service-account key, revoke the Vault token, and mark this CI run as suspected. who owns that CI pipeline? @maria?
maria: yeah that's mine, it's the integration-test-runner. looks like a test that prints environment for debugging. I'm opening a PR to remove the debug logging now. will also kick off a new run with sanitized env.
devops: commands to run now: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable 0123abcd --iam-account=ci-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com` then `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123abcd ...` also rotate any dependent workload identity bindings. for Vault: `vault token-revoke s.xxxxxx` and check `vault audit` for usage.
sec-oncall: I'm asking infra to collect audit logs (GCP admin activity + Vault audit device) for the last 72h to see token/key usage and any external IPs. Also we should assume the key was exfiltrated -> rotate any backend KMS-wrapped keys that used it as a wrapping key.
alex: question: our CI publishes artifacts to the same GCS bucket. should we rotate the bucket access?
maria: yes, rotate the bucket object ACLs and re-issue short-lived signed URLs. I'll revoke the bucket-level service account role until we finish investigation.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback triggered for pipeline/integration-test-runner at 1971234610.
:gear: action: disabled service key 0123abcd
jordan: quick note on Vault layout: that token maps to a long-lived policy 'ci-runner-default' which grants kv/data/read to secret/data/ci/* and transit/encrypt for a wrapping key. we need to rotate the transit key and rewrap secrets.
sec-oncall: agreed — plan: (1) disable compromised SA key and revoke token (done) (2) rotate Vault transit key: create new CMK in KMS, configure Vault to use new wrapping key and rewrap secrets via `vault write sys/rewrap` for affected paths (3) rotate any long-lived AWS/GCP creds referenced in those secrets (4) perform RBAC hardening: remove broad roles from CI service account and create a scoped short-lived workload identity with least-privilege (5) update CI to fetch secrets via Vault Agent with approved auth method and remove debug prints.
alex: operational questions: when rewrapping, which secrets paths are high priority? I'd say: `secret/data/prod/*`, `secret/data/dedicated/*`, and any keys under `transit/keys/` that are used by inference runtime. we should also mark all rewrapped secrets with metadata tag `rotated_by:1971234567`.
maria: I'll run an inventory scan for all secrets with policy `ci-runner-default` and post list in the ticket.
devops: for immediate containment, set Vault token TTL enforcement to max 1h for CI tokens and enable explicit token lookup on creation. also enable `audit` to send to remote logging for retention.
sec-oncall: also need to adjust RBAC: create a new GCP role `roles/ci.runner.readonly` with only `storage.objects.get` and `pubsub.publish` and remove `editor`-like roles from the SA. I'll coordinate with policy team for IAM change window.
jordan: low-friction mitigation: rotate the KMS customer-managed key (CMK) that Vault uses to wrap transit keys. steps: create new key version, rewrap transit keys, then disable old key version. confirm no running jobs depend on old key before disable.
alex: timeline: we should aim for containment in 60 minutes, rewrap and rotate in 6 hours, and full post-rotation audit in 24 hours. who's owning the 6-hour work? @maria?
maria: taking the 6-hour owner. I'll post ETA and progress in the incident ticket. starting inventory now.
infra-bot: audit-bot: requested logs exported to sec-s3-archive at 1971234620.

sec-oncall: action items captured: [jordan] evidence capture + paste redaction, [maria] rotate CI creds and PR to sanitize logs, [devops] revoke SA key + rotate bucket access, [alex] coordinate transit key rewrap and audit, [policy] RBAC role creation and heatmap. we'll have a quick sync on voice in 10.
jordan: uploading sanitized screenshots and the incident notes to the ticket now. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
